drills.q: Find the single element in an array where every other element appears exactly twice, in O(1) space.
drills.a: XOR-reduce the entire array; every paired duplicate cancels (a^a=0), leaving only the unpaired value.

drills.q: Find the missing number in an array containing n distinct values from [0, n].
drills.a: XOR every index 0..n with every array value; present numbers cancel with their index, leaving the missing one.

drills.q: Every element appears three times except one, which appears once. Derive an O(n) O(1)-space solution.
drills.a: For each of 32 bit positions, count how many numbers have that bit set; if the count isn't divisible by 3, the answer has that bit set. Reassemble bit by bit.

drills.q: Two distinct elements appear exactly once, all others appear exactly twice. Find both in O(n) time, O(1) space.
drills.a: XOR-reduce to get x^y, isolate its lowest set bit with v & -v, partition the array on that bit, XOR-reduce each partition to recover x and y separately.

drills.q: An array of 1..n has one number missing and one duplicated. Using only XOR and sum arithmetic, set up the system to solve for both.
drills.a: xor_all (array XOR full range 1..n) gives missing^duplicate; sum(1..n) - sum(array) gives missing-duplicate. Solve the resulting 2-equation system, or bit-partition and disambiguate using array membership.

drills.q: Design an O(32n) algorithm to find the maximum XOR of any two numbers in an array without sorting.
drills.a: Insert every number's bits (MSB to LSB) into a bitwise trie; for each number, walk the trie greedily choosing the opposite-bit child whenever available to maximize the running XOR.
